method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; a seat-neutral core (ei-core.l4, with Schedule I transcribed by script from the deposited text, and four regulative rules) and a seat layer (ei-seat.l4) that restates no rule; no REFUSE (hours below Schedule I answer an explicit no-benefits value, asserted); checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Employment Insurance Act, S.C. 1996, c. 23, and Employment Insurance Regulations, SOR/96-332, Justice Laws consolidation current to 2026-09-30 (Act last amended 2026-06-18; Regulations 2026-04-01), from justicecanada/laws-lois-xml commit 0507465393c224c0491fc8c17c88340217acc656, as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/S.C.-1996-c.-23.txt and SOR-96-332.txt. The maximum yearly insurable earnings, premium rate and regional rate of unemployment are inputs.

scope: From the seat of the insured person claiming regular benefits: s 6(1)-(2), s 7(2), s 7.1(1), s 12(2) and Schedule I, s 13, s 14(1)-(2), (4), s 17, s 29(b)-(c), s 30(1)-(2), (5)-(6), s 67 with s 82(2), Part VII ss 144-145; duties under s 50(4) with Regulations s 26, s 145(4) with s 146, s 44, s 112 as regulative rules. Out: special benefits, work-sharing, family supplement, seasonal-worker table, benefit period length and antedating, qualifying-period extension, disentitlement, earnings on claim and separation monies, self-employed and fishers, premium reduction and refunds, penalties and recovery. Read with subjects/ca/income-tax-act/ (s 144 income, repayment with the return, credits); cross-folder IMPORT is not possible.
seat: the insured person (employee) paying premiums and claiming regular benefits
